explainer.persistence.compression: the turn was stopped because another process was compressing this session. Your message should already be saved — please send it again after compression completes.
explainer.persistence.compression_closed: the turn was stopped because this session was rotated by context compression and its live continuation could not be adopted. The storage itself is healthy — refresh the client (or start a new turn) so it picks up the new session id, then send your message again.
explainer.persistence.corrupt:
the turn was stopped because the state database reported structural corruption (the transcript would have been lost on restart). Freeing disk space will not help. Recovery options:
1. Run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor --fix`
2. Stop the gateway, then recover with:
   hermes {profile_arg}sessions recover --source {db_path} --inspect-only
   (if it reports recoverable) hermes {profile_arg}sessions recover --source {db_path} --output recovered-state.db
   — recovery snapshots the damaged file first; do NOT run `sqlite3 ... ".recover"` against the live state.db, a vulnerable sqlite3 CLI can corrupt it further
3. Restore from a backup in {backups_dir}/
Then send your message again.
explainer.persistence.default: Hermes couldn't save this conversation, so it stopped rather than lose your messages. Possible causes: the drive is out of room, or another Hermes process is holding the database. Close other Hermes windows, run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor` to check storage, then send your message again.
explainer.persistence.deleted_wal: another Hermes process still holds an old copy of the session database's write-ahead log, so Hermes stopped writing to keep the file safe and this message was not saved (a copy is kept in {home}/sessions/). Nothing is lost. Quit every Hermes process on this profile (Desktop app, `hermes {profile_arg}gateway stop`, dashboard, cron), run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor` — it names any process still holding the log — then start Hermes again and send your message once more. Do not run `doctor --fix` or delete any state.db files while they run. Guide: {recovery_docs}
explainer.persistence.disk: Hermes couldn't save this conversation to disk, so it stopped rather than lose your messages. The disk is probably full: free some space (or fix the permissions on {home}/state.db), then send your message again.
explainer.persistence.fts_index: the turn was stopped because the session search index (FTS5) is corrupt and could not be detached, so this message was not saved. The message store itself is not damaged: do not run recovery tools or restore a backup. Run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor --fix` (or restart Hermes, which repairs the index on open), then send your message again.
explainer.persistence.locked: the turn was stopped because session storage was busy (another Hermes process was writing to the state database). Your message should already be saved — please send it again in a moment.
explainer.persistence.replaced: the session database file was replaced while Hermes was running, so this message was not saved (a copy is kept in {home}/sessions/). Stop Hermes (`hermes {profile_arg}gateway stop`), run `hermes {profile_arg}doctor` — not `hermes {profile_arg}doctor --fix`, which would repair the wrong file in place — then start it again and send your message once more. Advanced recovery steps are in the log.

gateway.topic.help:
/topic — enable multi-session DM mode (one bot, many parallel chats)

Usage:
  /topic             Enable topic mode, or show status if already on
  /topic help        Show this message
  /topic off         Disable topic mode and clear topic bindings
  /topic <id>        Inside a topic: restore a previous session by ID

How it works:
1. Run /topic once in this DM — Hermes checks BotFather Threads
   Settings are enabled and flips on multi-session mode.
2. Tap All Messages at the top of the bot and send any message.
   Telegram creates a new topic for that message; each topic is
   an independent Hermes session (fresh history, fresh context).
3. The root DM becomes a system lobby — send /topic, /status,
   /help, /usage there. Normal prompts go in a topic.
4. /new inside a topic resets just that topic's session.
5. /topic <id> inside a topic restores an old session into it.

tips.t001: /bg <prompt> runs a task in a separate session while your current one stays free; /btw <question> answers a side question about this conversation without interrupting it.
tips.t002: /branch forks the current session so you can explore a different direction without losing progress.
tips.t003: /compress manually compresses conversation context when things get long.
tips.t004: /rollback lists filesystem checkpoints — restore files the agent modified to any prior state.
tips.t005: /rollback diff 2 previews what changed since checkpoint 2 without restoring anything.
tips.t006: /rollback 2 src/file.py restores a single file from a specific checkpoint.
tips.t007: /title "my project" names your session — resume it later with /resume or hermes -c.
tips.t008: /resume picks up where you left off in a previously named session.
tips.t009: /queue <prompt> queues a message for the next turn without interrupting the current one.
tips.t010: /undo removes the last user/assistant exchange from the conversation.
tips.t011: /retry resends your last message — useful when the agent's response wasn't quite right.
tips.t012: /verbose cycles tool progress display: off → new → all → verbose.
tips.t013: /reasoning high increases the model's thinking depth. /reasoning show displays the reasoning.
tips.t014: /fast toggles priority processing for faster API responses (provider-dependent).
tips.t015: /yolo skips all dangerous command approval prompts for the rest of the session.
tips.t016: /model lets you switch models mid-session — try /model sonnet or /model gpt-5.
tips.t018: /personality pirate sets a fun personality — 14 built-in options from kawaii to shakespeare.
tips.t019: /skin changes the CLI theme — try ares, mono, slate, poseidon, or charizard.
tips.t020: /statusbar toggles a persistent bar showing model, tokens, context fill %, cost, and duration.
tips.t021: /tools disable browser temporarily removes browser tools for the current session.
tips.t022: /browser connect attaches browser tools to your running Chromium-family browser via CDP.
tips.t023: /plugins lists installed plugins and their status.
tips.t024: /cron manages scheduled tasks — set up recurring prompts with delivery to any platform.
tips.t025: /reload-mcp hot-reloads MCP server configuration without restarting.
tips.t026: /usage shows token usage, cost breakdown, and session duration.
tips.t027: /insights shows usage analytics for the last 30 days.
tips.t028: /paste checks your clipboard for an image and attaches it to your next message.
tips.t029: /profile shows which profile is active and its home directory.
tips.t030: /config shows your current configuration at a glance.
tips.t031: /stop kills all running background processes spawned by the agent.
tips.t032: @file:path/to/file.py injects file contents directly into your message.
tips.t033: @file:main.py:10-50 injects only lines 10-50 of a file.
tips.t035: @diff injects your unstaged git changes into the message.
tips.t036: @staged injects your staged git changes (git diff --staged).
tips.t037: @git:5 injects the last 5 commits with full patches.
tips.t038: @url:https://example.com fetches and injects a web page's content.
tips.t039: Typing @ triggers filesystem path completion — navigate to any file interactively.
tips.t040: Combine multiple references: "Review @file:main.py and @file:test.py for consistency."
tips.t041: Alt+Enter inserts a newline for multi-line input. (Windows Terminal intercepts Alt+Enter — use Ctrl+Enter instead.)
tips.t042: Ctrl+C interrupts the agent. Double-press within 2 seconds to force exit.
tips.t043: Ctrl+Z suspends Hermes to the background — run fg in your shell to resume.
tips.t044: Tab accepts auto-suggestion ghost text or autocompletes slash commands.
tips.t045: Type a new message while the agent is working to interrupt and redirect it.
tips.t046: Alt+V pastes an image from your clipboard into the conversation.
tips.t047: Pasting 5+ lines auto-saves to a file and inserts a compact reference instead.
tips.t048: hermes -c resumes your most recent CLI session. hermes -c "project name" resumes by title.
tips.t049: hermes -w creates an isolated git worktree — perfect for parallel agent workflows.
tips.t050: hermes -w -q "Fix issue #42" combines worktree isolation with a one-shot query.
tips.t051: hermes chat -t web,terminal enables only specific toolsets for a focused session.
tips.t052: hermes chat -s github-pr-workflow preloads a skill at launch.
tips.t053: hermes chat -q "query" runs a single non-interactive query and exits.
tips.t054: hermes chat --max-turns 1000 overrides the default 500-iteration limit per turn.
tips.t055: hermes chat --checkpoints enables filesystem snapshots before every destructive file change.
tips.t056: hermes --yolo bypasses all dangerous command approval prompts for the entire session.
tips.t057: hermes chat --source telegram tags the session for filtering in hermes sessions list.
tips.t058: hermes -p work chat runs under a specific profile without changing your default.
tips.t059: hermes doctor --fix diagnoses and auto-repairs config and dependency issues.
tips.t060: hermes dump outputs a compact setup summary — great for bug reports.
tips.t061: hermes config set KEY VALUE auto-routes secrets to .env and everything else to config.yaml.
tips.t062: hermes config edit opens config.yaml in your default editor.
tips.t063: hermes config check scans for missing or stale configuration options.
tips.t064: hermes sessions browse opens an interactive session picker with search.
tips.t065: hermes sessions stats shows session counts by platform and database size.
tips.t066: hermes sessions prune --older-than 30 cleans up old sessions.
tips.t067: hermes skills search react --source skills-sh searches the skills.sh public directory.
tips.t068: hermes skills check scans installed hub skills for upstream updates.
tips.t069: hermes skills tap add myorg/skills-repo adds a custom GitHub skill source.
tips.t070: hermes skills snapshot export setup.json exports your skill configuration for backup or sharing.
tips.t071: hermes mcp add github --command npx adds MCP servers from the command line.
tips.t072: hermes mcp-serve runs Hermes itself as an MCP server for other agents.
tips.t073: hermes auth add lets you add multiple API keys for credential pool rotation.
tips.t074: hermes completion bash >> ~/.bashrc enables tab completion for all commands and profiles.
tips.t075: hermes logs -f follows agent.log in real time. --level WARNING --since 1h filters output.
tips.t076: hermes backup creates a zip backup of your entire Hermes home directory.
tips.t077: hermes profile create coder creates an isolated profile that becomes its own command.
tips.t078: hermes profile create work --clone copies your current config and keys to a new profile.
tips.t079: hermes update syncs new bundled skills to ALL profiles automatically.
tips.t080: hermes gateway install sets up Hermes as a system service (systemd/launchd).
tips.t081: hermes memory setup lets you configure an external memory provider (Honcho, Mem0, etc.).
tips.t082: hermes webhook subscribe creates event-driven webhook routes with HMAC validation.
tips.t083: Save money: hermes tools disables unused tools, hermes skills config trims skills down.
tips.t084: /reasoning low or /reasoning minimal cuts thinking depth below the default (medium) — faster, cheaper responses.
tips.t085: hermes models routes vision, compression, and aux tasks to cheaper models — cuts background token cost 85%+ without downgrading your main chat model.
tips.t086: Set display.bell_on_complete: true in config.yaml to hear a bell when long tasks finish.
tips.t087: Set display.streaming: true to see tokens appear in real time as the model generates.
tips.t088: Set display.show_reasoning: true to watch the model's chain-of-thought reasoning.
tips.t089: Set display.compact: true to reduce whitespace in output for denser information.
tips.t090: Set display.busy_input_mode: queue to queue messages instead of interrupting the agent, or steer to inject them mid-run via /steer.
tips.t091: Set display.resume_display: minimal to skip the full conversation recap on session resume.
tips.t092: Set compression.threshold: 0.50 to control when auto-compression fires (default: 50% of context).
tips.t093: Set agent.max_turns: 1000 to let the agent take more tool-calling steps per turn.
tips.t094: Set file_read_max_chars: 200000 to increase the max content per read_file call.
tips.t095: Set approvals.mode: smart to let an LLM auto-approve safe commands and auto-deny dangerous ones.
tips.t096: Set fallback_model in config.yaml to automatically fail over to a backup provider.
tips.t097: Set privacy.redact_pii: true to hash user IDs and phone numbers before sending to the LLM.
tips.t098: Set browser.headed: true to watch the local Chromium window while the agent browses.
tips.t099: Set worktree: true in config.yaml to always create a git worktree (same as hermes -w).
tips.t100: Set security.website_blocklist.enabled: true to block specific domains from web tools.

tips.t363: HERMES_OPTIONAL_SKILLS=name1,name2 auto-installs extra optional-catalog skills on first run per profile.
tips.t364: HERMES_BUNDLED_SKILLS points at a custom bundled-skill tree — used by Homebrew and Nix packaging.
tips.t365: HERMES_DUMP_REQUEST_STDOUT=1 dumps every API request payload to stdout instead of log files.
tips.t366: HERMES_OAUTH_TRACE=1 logs redacted OAuth token exchange and refresh attempts for debugging provider auth.
tips.t367: HERMES_STREAM_RETRIES (default 3) controls mid-stream reconnect attempts on transient network errors.
tips.t368: HERMES_GATEWAY_BUSY_ACK_ENABLED=false silences the ⚡/⏳/⏩ ack messages when a user messages a busy agent.
tips.t369: HERMES_AGENT_NOTIFY_INTERVAL (default 180s) sets how often the gateway pings with progress on long turns.
tips.t370: HERMES_RESTART_DRAIN_TIMEOUT (default 900s) caps how long /restart waits for in-flight runs before forcing.
tips.t371: HERMES_CHECKPOINT_TIMEOUT (default 30s) caps filesystem checkpoint creation — raise it on huge monorepos.
tips.t372: image_gen.model in config.yaml picks the FAL model: flux-2/klein, gpt-image-2, nano-banana-pro, and more.
tips.t373: image_gen.provider routes image generation through a plugin (OpenAI Images, Codex, FAL) instead of the default.
tips.t374: AUXILIARY_VISION_BASE_URL + AUXILIARY_VISION_API_KEY point vision analysis at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
tips.t375: API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME customizes the model name on /v1/models — essential for multi-profile Open WebUI setups.
tips.t376: Dashboard plugins are served from /dashboard-plugins/<name>/ — drop files into ~/.hermes/dashboard-plugins/.
tips.t377: --source tool chats are excluded from hermes sessions list by default — set --source explicitly to see them.
